short: Agricultural pioneer whose invention of the seed drill helped spark the British Agricultural Revolution.
full:
Jethro Tull was a gentleman farmer who became deeply frustrated with the traditional, wasteful method of sowing seeds by scattering them broadly by hand. In 1701, he invented a mechanical seed drill drawn by a horse, which sowed seeds in neat, evenly spaced rows at a specific depth, dramatically improving germination rates and crop yields.

He also advocated for the frequent hoeing of soil between the rows to destroy weeds and aerate the earth, principles he detailed in his influential 1731 book, The New Horse-Houghing Husbandry. Although his ideas faced considerable initial resistance from farm labourers and traditionalists, his mechanised, systematic approach eventually transformed British farming and supported the demographic explosion of the eighteenth century.
